## Context
The 884-unit hardening oracle invokes production `_convert` once per unit. `_convert` currently resolves `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s` on every invocation. A runtime trace on current origin/main d05bf2bc1be observed 100 Pandoc plus 102 `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` subprocesses for 100 conversions; resolving once at the render-pass boundary preserved identical outputs and reduced the trace to 100 Pandoc plus 3 one-time root probes. The prior 884-unit trace observed 1,770 total Popen calls (884 Pandoc + 886 root discovery). This is separate from the copied legacy oracle removed by absolute-diplomatic-snowyowl.

## Contract and prior disposition
- Preserve all real Pandoc calls, corpus units, byte expectations, timeout configurability, per-unit fallback, timeout, and process-group reap behavior.
- absolute-diplomatic-snowyowl approved immutable outputs only for the copied legacy side and retained all 884 real production conversions. harmless-wavy-osprey approved session-scoped sharing that reduced duplicate work, while coercive-paediatric-bug rejected parallelism that does not reduce aggregate runner usage. No tracker ticket rejects render-pass configuration injection.
- Full replacement of product Pandoc calls remains out of scope because ADR 0095 requires the real pinned boundary in every conversion assertion.

## OSS consensus research (2026-08-14)
All three surveyed projects are active, unarchived, and popular: Django (88,426 stars; pushed 2026-08-13) lazily resolves each setting and caches it in `LazySettings.__dict__`; Black (41,804 stars; pushed 2026-08-10) reads pyproject configuration at CLI setup and passes resolved `mode` into multi-file workers; pytest (14,416 stars; pushed 2026-08-12) exposes its resolved Config as a session-scoped `pytestconfig` fixture. Consensus is 3/3 for resolving loop/session invariants once and passing them to repeated work.

## Plan
1. Add a held-out behavioral oracle proving one render pass resolves timeout once while every renderable unit still crosses `_convert`, and freeze the contract before implementation.
2. Resolve timeout once in `render_markdown_to_wiki`, pass it through `_render_unit`, and add an optional private `_convert` timeout parameter so direct callers retain safe default behavior.
3. Make the 884-unit direct hardening loop resolve timeout once outside the loop and pass it to `_convert`; keep exact expected bytes and all real Pandoc invocations.
4. Run held-out RED -> fixer -> GREEN, defect-seeded RED, focused hardening/corpus tests, lint, typecheck, and paired subprocess/timing measurement.
5. Push through Gerrit; merge only after LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, no unresolved comments, then record CI and runner savings. Back-out is a Gerrit revert restoring per-call timeout resolution.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A render pass resolves `dc_pandoc_timeout_s` once, not once per renderable unit.
- [ ] The 884-unit hardening oracle launches all 884 real production Pandoc conversions and no per-unit Git-root discovery.
- [ ] Runtime timeout configuration remains observable at the documented render-pass/direct-call boundary.
- [ ] Timeout, fallback, stdin, byte-equivalence, and process-group reap contracts retain equivalent behavioral coverage.
- [ ] Held-out RED/GREEN and exact defect-seeded RED are recorded.
- [ ] Before/after subprocess counts and wall time quantify savings without claiming more than the evidence.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, LLM-Review +1, and Verified +1 pass before merge.
- [ ] Final report cites OSS sources and prior-ticket dispositions.
